trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.missableNote: Cannot be missed: it unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned.
trophies.guide: The platinum itself. It pops on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all on your account, so there is nothing separate to hunt. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap in this guide: story first, side strands and activities alongside, the 100% checklist after the credits, then a short clean-up sweep. Expect a long run — published roadmaps put the full platinum at roughly 200 hours, with almost all of that time going into 100% completion rather than difficulty.
steps: Follow the four roadmap stages in order and tick trophies off as they land.
Keep cheats off for the whole run: guides agree cheats disable trophies and saving.
When only a handful remain, use the filters here to list what is left by kind and grade.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy: awarded by the opening mission itself, so it cannot be skipped.
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Gone Fishing, the opening mission of the story. Simply start a new game and play the prologue through to its end; the trophy lands as the mission closes. Because there is no mission replay, this is also a good moment to learn the basics — driving, cover and the partner system — before the open world fully opens up.
steps: Start the story and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing.
Follow the on-screen objectives until the mission complete screen appears.
The trophy unlocks automatically at mission end.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy, but Chapter 1 holds the game's one possible missable — see Positive Mental Attitude before you finish this chapter.
trophies.guide: Awarded when Chapter 1 ends. Play the chapter's story missions in order and the trophy pops at the chapter break. One caution belongs here rather than later: during this chapter, after the mission Down to Earth, a short optional meditation scene at the protagonist's house is the only content guides flag as possibly missable, so do that scene before you close the chapter (details under Positive Mental Attitude). Keeping a manual save at the chapter's end is cheap insurance, since the game offers no mission replay.
steps: Play Chapter 1's story missions in order.
After Down to Earth, take the morning meditation invitation at the house before moving on.
Finish the chapter's final mission; the trophy unlocks at the chapter break.
Keep a manual save from the end of the chapter in a spare slot.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy: cannot be missed while progressing the campaign.
trophies.guide: Awarded when Chapter 2 ends; the name is shown exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included. Keep following the story markers and finish the chapter's closing mission. By now the map and activity icons are opening up — it is worth sampling each new activity type once as it appears, which quietly banks progress toward Master of None, and entering every new vehicle you drive for Whip It Good.
steps: Continue the story through Chapter 2's missions.
Try each new activity icon once as it unlocks, and enter new vehicles to register them.
Finish the chapter finale; the trophy unlocks automatically.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy: cannot be missed while progressing the campaign.
trophies.guide: Awarded at the end of Chapter 3, the midpoint of the five-chapter story. Play the chapter through and the trophy is yours. The middle chapters are the best window to advance the stranger strands that later pay out their own finale trophies, because those characters are active now; guides note some quest givers pause during certain story beats but return afterwards, so nothing here is lost permanently.
steps: Play Chapter 3's story missions to the chapter finale.
Between story missions, advance any open stranger strands on the map.
The trophy unlocks when the chapter closes.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy: cannot be missed while progressing the campaign.
trophies.guide: Awarded when Chapter 4 ends, leaving only the final chapter between you and the credits. Finish the chapter's missions in order. Before pushing into the finale, tidy up anything character-based that you have left half done, and make a fresh manual save at the chapter break — roadmaps recommend holding saves at chapter starts and ends precisely because there is no mission replay to fall back on.
steps: Complete Chapter 4's story missions.
Round off open stranger strands and activity first-tries.
Save manually at the chapter break, then start the final chapter.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy: the campaign's final mission awards it directly.
trophies.guide: The gold story trophy, awarded for completing the final mission of the campaign. Play the last chapter through its finale and the trophy pops with the ending. Finishing the story is also the gateway to the real platinum work: the 100% completion checklist only becomes fully visible after the credits, and free-roam continues afterwards, so every remaining trophy in this guide can still be earned from here.
steps: Play the final chapter through to the last mission.
Complete the final mission; the gold trophy unlocks with the ending.
After the credits, open Progress to reveal the 100% checklist and move to roadmap stage 3.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy tied to a named campaign mission; awarded as part of normal story progress.
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the story mission Breakfast Run. It arrives as part of the campaign flow, so no detour is needed: follow the story markers, finish the mission's objectives, and the trophy unlocks on the mission complete screen. Treat every named-mission trophy in this block the same way — they are a checklist of story beats, not separate hunts.
steps: Reach Breakfast Run in the story sequence.
Complete its objectives and reach the mission complete screen.
The trophy unlocks automatically.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy tied to a named campaign set-piece; awarded through story progress.
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing The Cartel Heist, one of the campaign's set-piece missions. Play it as the story presents it and finish every objective; the trophy lands at mission end. Heist-style missions are also a natural place to practise the partner coordination that two free-roam trophies (Hot Together and Retail Therapy) later ask for outside the story.
steps: Reach The Cartel Heist in the story sequence.
Work through the heist objectives with your partner.
The trophy unlocks on completion.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy tied to a named campaign mission; awarded through story progress.
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the story mission Child's Play. Like the other named-mission trophies, it is earned simply by playing the campaign in order — no optional condition is attached in the official description. Keep progressing the story and it will unlock on the mission complete screen.
steps: Reach Child's Play in the story sequence.
Finish the mission's objectives.
The trophy unlocks automatically at mission end.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy tied to a named campaign mission; awarded through story progress.
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing the story mission Headliners. Progress the campaign until this mission appears, play it through, and the trophy unlocks when it ends. Nothing in the official description adds a side condition, so the only way to delay it is to delay the story itself.
steps: Reach Headliners in the story sequence.
Complete the mission.
The trophy unlocks at mission end.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy tied to a named campaign mission; awarded through story progress.
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing VCIA Takedown, a story mission centred on the airport authority. Play it when the campaign offers it and finish its objectives for the trophy. The airport setting is worth remembering: a separate free-roam trophy, Catch Me If You Can, also revolves around VCIA, so the familiarity you build here pays off later.
steps: Reach VCIA Takedown in the story sequence.
Complete the takedown objectives.
The trophy unlocks at mission end.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.missableNote: Story trophy tied to a named campaign mission; awarded through story progress.
trophies.guide: Awarded for completing Operation Savage Glory, a named story operation. As with the rest of this block, the trophy is a story checkpoint: reach the mission, finish it, and the unlock follows. If you are pacing the roadmap, these named missions are the spine of stage 1 — everything else in the guide hangs off finishing them.
steps: Reach Operation Savage Glory in the story sequence.
Complete the operation's objectives.
The trophy unlocks at mission end.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.missableNote: Cannot be missed: free-roam continues after the story and the checklist stays open.
trophies.guide: The gold that dominates the platinum: reach 100% on the in-game completion checklist. The full checklist only appears after the story credits, although everything you did earlier already counts toward it. Guides describe the thresholds as generous — you need most of the game's systems rather than literally every last item (for example, only part of the collectible card sets and a share of the challenges are required) — but the sheer breadth makes this the longest trophy in the game and the one every roadmap calls the hardest. Work it from the Progress menu category by category instead of wandering.
steps: Finish the story, then open Progress > 100% Completion to see the full checklist.
Clear the big blocks first: required robberies and operations, shooting ranges and races.
Sweep collectible categories next, using each category's in-game counter.
Finish the remaining percentage with challenges and activities until the checklist reads 100%.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list
KeenGamer — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Platinum Roadmap

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: stunts stay available in free-roam and far more exist than the trophy needs.
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunt jumps across Leonida. Guides count roughly 397 stunt locations in the game, so you need a little over half of them — there is comfortable slack if a few jumps refuse to register. A stunt only counts when the game registers a clean landing, so favour a sturdy, fast vehicle and a straight run-up. Your running total is visible in the Progress menu, which makes this an easy background trophy to chip away at while travelling between other objectives.
steps: Check your current stunt count under Progress before starting a session.
Pick a fast, durable vehicle and work stunt icons area by area.
Land cleanly on all wheels for the jump to register.
Repeat across districts until the counter reaches 250.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list
Push Square — GTA 6 Trophy Guide and Roadmap

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: activity types remain available after the story.
trophies.guide: Sample every one of the game's 9 activity types at least once. You do not need to win or even finish most of them — a single genuine attempt at each type registers it. The practical approach is to try each activity the first time its icon appears during the story, rather than hunting types down later. If the trophy has not popped by the endgame, open the Progress menu and compare the activity list against what you remember trying; the missing type is usually the one whose icon you always drove past.
steps: Each time a new activity icon type appears on the map, try it once straight away.
Keep a rough note of types tried until all 9 are covered.
If it has not unlocked by the endgame, audit the Progress menu's activity list and sample the gap.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: range challenges can be retried freely.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the precision trophy of the set: each challenge scores accuracy and speed, and gold demands a near-clean run. Practise one weapon class until its handling is familiar before chasing its golds, learn where targets appear in each layout, and retry immediately while the pattern is fresh — challenges can be repeated as often as you like. Progress per challenge is shown at the range, so work range by range rather than cherry-picking.
steps: Visit a shooting range and note the medal you hold for each of the 42 challenges.
Practise one weapon class at a time until its gold feels repeatable.
Replay challenges instantly after a failed gold attempt to keep the target pattern fresh.
Move to the next range only when its board is all gold.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: races stay available and can be retried.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at each of the 14 locations. Unlike participation trophies, this one asks for outright wins, but the races are short and endlessly retryable. Learn a course with one exploratory run, then attack it: hold smooth lines through the gates, avoid clipping scenery (a crash costs more time than a slightly wider turn), and restart the moment a run goes badly rather than finishing a lost race.
steps: Fly each new course once to learn its gate order.
Restart immediately after any crash or missed gate.
Bank the win, then move to the next of the 14 locations.
Track remaining locations from the map and Progress menu.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: races remain available in free-roam.
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different is the operative word, so repeating one easy race twenty times does not count. Spread your wins across the race types the game offers and across districts. Bring the fastest vehicle the event allows, learn each route with a first attempt, and treat early losses as scouting. Many of these wins will happen naturally while you work on 100% completion, since races sit on that checklist too.
steps: Enter races in different districts and of different types.
Use your first run on a route to learn it, then rerun for the win.
Keep count in the Progress menu until 20 distinct wins are banked.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: the challenge can be attempted again.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in one of his fishing challenges. Find Cal's fishing challenge, accept it, and out-catch him within its rules. Practise the fishing mechanics first in free-roam — casting, bite timing and reeling — so the challenge itself is about the fish rather than the controls. If an attempt fails, the challenge can be taken again, so treat the first try as a rehearsal and adjust your spot and timing on the second.
steps: Practise fishing in free-roam until casting and reeling feel automatic.
Start Cal's fishing challenge.
Fish the most productive spot you found and land your catches cleanly.
Outscore Cal before the challenge ends; retry if needed.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: arcade machines stay where they are.
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Find an arcade cabinet in the world, start its game, and play it through to a genuine completion rather than quitting at the first screen. Pick the shortest or simplest cabinet you find — the trophy asks for a completion, not a high score — and this pairs naturally with Master of None, since an arcade visit also registers the arcade activity type.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet and interact with it.
Choose the shortest game on offer.
Play it through to completion without quitting.
The trophy unlocks as the game ends.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.missableNote: Watch: strand givers can pause during story beats. Guides agree trophy quest givers return after the story, so finish the strand in free-roam if it pauses.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's strand by completing his final mission. Work Andy's missions whenever his marker is available, in order, until the strand's closing mission appears, then complete it for the trophy. Some secondary sources warn that stranger chains have availability windows tied to story progress, while the larger guides report that trophy-related quest givers are all still available in post-story free-roam — the honest summary is: do the strand when it is offered, and do not panic if it pauses mid-story.
steps: Accept Andy's first mission when his marker appears.
Complete each follow-up mission in the strand as it unlocks.
Play the strand's final mission to its end.
The trophy unlocks on completion of that finale.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.missableNote: Watch: Kenton is named by guides as a giver who becomes temporarily unavailable during parts of the story — he returns afterwards, so the trophy is delayed, not lost.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's strand by completing his final mission. Kenton is specifically mentioned in roadmap notes as a quest giver who can become temporarily unavailable while the story moves through certain beats; the same notes confirm he comes back, and every trophy quest giver is present again in post-story free-roam. So the method is patience plus persistence: advance his missions when offered, and if his marker vanishes mid-story, continue the campaign and check back after the next chapter.
steps: Start Kenton's strand when his marker appears.
Complete his missions in order as they unlock.
If his marker disappears during a story beat, progress the story and return later.
Complete his final mission; the trophy unlocks at its end.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.missableNote: Watch: as with the other strands, availability can pause with story progress; the giver returns in free-roam.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's strand by completing his final mission. Take Billy's missions in order whenever they are offered and see the strand through to its finale. As with the other character strands in this set, treat a disappearing marker as a pause rather than a failure — post-story free-roam restores access to trophy quest givers, so the finale can always be reached eventually.
steps: Accept Billy's opening mission.
Work through the strand's missions in order.
Complete the final mission of the strand.
The trophy unlocks on completion.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: Watch: it aggregates the strand finales, so it inherits their availability pauses — but strands remain finishable after the story.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. A strand only counts when you finish its whole chain, not when you merely meet the character. The five named finale trophies in this guide (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone) are five of the strands, so chasing those trophies puts you most of the way here; find three more strands on the map and finish them too. Note the strands are not part of the 100% checklist — this silver is its own separate piece of work.
steps: Finish the five named character strands (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone).
Pick up three further stranger strands from map markers.
Complete each strand's final mission, not just its opener.
The silver unlocks when the eighth strand is completed.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list
KeenGamer — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Platinum Roadmap

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.missableNote: Watch: strand availability can pause with story progress; the finale stays reachable in free-roam.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's strand by completing his final mission. Follow Randy's mission chain from its first marker to the closing job, completing each step as it unlocks. The strand also counts as one of the eight needed for Strangers & Freaks, so finishing it does double duty. If the chain stalls during a story-heavy stretch, progress the campaign and return — the giver remains available afterwards.
steps: Start Randy's strand at his marker.
Complete each mission in the chain in order.
Finish the strand's final mission.
The trophy unlocks, and the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.missableNote: Watch: strand availability can pause with story progress; the finale stays reachable in free-roam.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's strand by completing his final mission. Work Tyrone's chain in order from first marker to finale. Like the other four named strands, this one also feeds the Strangers & Freaks count, so it is efficient to run these strands during the story rather than leaving all five for the endgame.
steps: Accept Tyrone's first mission.
Complete the strand's missions as they unlock.
Play the final mission to completion.
The trophy unlocks at the finale's end.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missableNote: POSSIBLY MISSABLE — the one flagged trophy. A Chapter 1 meditation at the house balcony (after Down to Earth) disappears after Chapter 1. Whether the trophy's counter requires it is unconfirmed, but doing it costs two minutes: do it.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida — 18 meditations in all. This is the only trophy the big guides flag as potentially missable, and the risk is specific: in Chapter 1, after the mission Down to Earth, your partner can be found at the house in the morning announcing she will meditate on the balcony; follow her and accept, and that short scene adds one to this trophy's counter before it vanishes for good at the chapter's end. Whether that one meditation is strictly required is honestly unconfirmed — the guide author who reported it did the scene and later earned the trophy — so the safe play is simply to do it. The remaining spots are ordinary world locations you can visit at any time, with some spots used by both protagonists.
steps: In Chapter 1, after Down to Earth, return to the house in the morning.
Follow your partner to the balcony and accept the meditation prompt.
After Chapter 1, visit every remaining meditation spot on the map and meditate at each.
Check the counter under Progress until all 18 are registered.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.missableNote: Watch: it hangs off Bret's strand, whose availability follows the same pause-and-return pattern as other quest givers.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Take Bret's hunting request, track the specific animal it names, and bring the hunt to a successful end. Learn the hunting basics first — tracking signs and a clean, quick kill — on ordinary animals, so the unique hunt itself is not your first attempt. Bret's strand also connects to the wider hunting content that the 100% checklist draws on, so time spent here is not wasted.
steps: Accept Bret's hunting request.
Practise tracking and clean kills on common animals first.
Track the unique animal the request names.
Complete the hunt and return to Bret; the trophy unlocks.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list
KeenGamer — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Platinum Roadmap

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: cards remain collectible in free-roam, and more sets exist than the trophy needs.
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets. The game holds more sets than this trophy asks for — guides count 18 sets in total, with 15 of them feeding the 100% checklist — so pick the three sets you are closest to finishing and close those out first. Cards are scattered through the world, including some inside buildings you visit during the story; a few magazine-style collectibles sit in story locations that later close, but guides note those items also spawn elsewhere, so no set is permanently blockable. Track set progress in the Progress menu and hunt by set, not at random.
steps: Open the collectibles page under Progress and note your closest sets.
Hunt the missing cards of one set at a time.
Complete a set, then repeat for two more.
The silver unlocks when the third set is complete.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list
Push Square — GTA 6 Trophy Guide and Roadmap

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: locations stay available; this is a pure accumulation trophy.
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK interaction at 100 different locations. This is a volume trophy: the interaction is quick, the locations are plentiful, and the only real work is remembering to do it whenever you pass a fresh spot instead of saving all 100 for one tedious sweep. Weave it into other travel — stunt runs and card hunting cross the same map — and check your count under Progress so you know how the background progress is adding up.
steps: Learn the WAiNK prompt the first time a location offers it.
Use it at every new location you visit while doing other objectives.
Check the Progress counter periodically.
Top up with a dedicated sweep if you reach the endgame short of 100.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: challenges remain available and more exist than the trophy requires.
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. The game offers more challenges than this — the 100% checklist itself draws on a large share of them — so you can favour the challenge types that suit how you play and skip the most awkward ones. Challenges accumulate naturally if you accept them as they appear during the story and the 100% sweep; if you reach the endgame short, the Progress menu shows which challenge categories still have easy completions left.
steps: Accept challenges as they appear during story and free-roam play.
Favour the challenge types you complete most reliably.
Track the running total under Progress.
Sweep the easiest remaining categories until you reach 50.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: it can be set up in free-roam at any time with your partner present.
trophies.guide: While your partner is with you, reach a 4-star wanted level and then lose it completely — the stars must fully clear, not merely drop. Set it up deliberately in free-roam: commit enough mayhem in your partner's company to hit four stars, then break line of sight and keep moving through cover, alleys and vehicle swaps until the search ends. Dying or being arrested voids the attempt, so prioritise distance over fighting once the fourth star lands.
steps: Free-roam with your partner accompanying you.
Raise your wanted level to 4 stars.
Break line of sight and keep relocating until the search starts to fade.
Stay hidden until all stars clear; the trophy unlocks on the clean escape.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: the chain can be attempted in free-roam whenever your partner is with you.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in an unbroken chain with your partner, keeping a wanted level alive the whole time. The catch is the chain: your wanted level must never fully clear between shops, so dawdling until the heat dies resets your progress. Plan a tight route of three nearby shops before you start, rob the first, drive straight to the second while still wanted, then the third, and only shake the police once the third robbery is done.
steps: Scout three shops close together and park a fast car outside the first.
With your partner present, rob shop one and keep the wanted level active.
Drive directly to shop two and rob it before the stars clear.
Repeat at shop three; the trophy unlocks once the third robbery registers.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: new vehicles keep appearing in traffic throughout the game.
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — a vehicle counts when you get in and drive it for the first time. This accumulates almost by itself if you make a habit of stealing variety instead of always returning to one favourite car: every new model you sit in moves the counter. Deliberate variety speeds it up — visit different districts, since traffic pools differ by area and wealth, and check parked cars in lots and driveways, which often hold models that rarely spawn in traffic.
steps: Get into every unfamiliar vehicle model you see and drive it briefly.
Rotate districts to meet different traffic pools.
Check car parks and driveways for rarer parked models.
Watch the Progress counter until it reaches 100.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: any crowded firefight in free-roam or a robbery offers the setup.
trophies.guide: Drop 5 enemies during one activation of Combat Focus, the slow-motion aiming state. The trick is preparation, not reflexes: do not trigger Focus the moment a fight starts. Instead, let a group of five or more enemies gather in the open — gang operations and robbery escapes are reliable setups — line up your shots, then activate Focus and work through the group before it ends. A weapon with a generous magazine saves reload time you cannot afford mid-Focus.
steps: Find or provoke a fight with at least five enemies in the open.
Let them group up; do not activate Combat Focus yet.
Activate Focus and take down five enemies before it expires.
The trophy unlocks on the fifth takedown in that single use.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: the airport can be revisited in free-roam.
trophies.guide: Leave VCIA — the airport — in a way no timetable allows: in practice, steal an aircraft and take off without clearance. Get onto the airfield in free-roam, reach a usable plane before security overwhelms you, and get airborne. Expect a wanted level for the attempt, so pick your aircraft first and run straight for it rather than sightseeing on the tarmac. The story mission VCIA Takedown familiarises you with the layout beforehand.
steps: Head to VCIA in free-roam and get airside.
Pick the nearest usable aircraft and go straight to it.
Board it and take off without clearance.
The trophy unlocks as your unscheduled departure registers.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: Rhinos appear at high wanted levels and in late-game encounters, so chances recur.
trophies.guide: The official description is a joke rather than instructions — it hints at Rhinos, the game's tanks, and heat. Read plainly, this is the tank encounter trophy: get into a confrontation involving a Rhino and come through it. Rhinos enter play when wanted levels run very high and in heavy late-game encounters, so the natural route is to push a wanted level to its ceiling in an area where you have room to manoeuvre, engage the armour that arrives on your own terms, and survive the exchange. Because the description is deliberately vague, treat any Rhino encounter after the story as an opportunity and keep a save beforehand.
steps: Raise a wanted level to its highest tier in open ground.
Engage the Rhino armour that responds, using cover and heavy weapons.
Survive and resolve the encounter.
If it does not pop, repeat at the next Rhino encounter — they recur at maximum heat.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: jewelry stores can be attempted again; a failed attempt only means retrying cleanly.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store with detection never triggering. Stealth is the whole trophy: case the store first, note staff and camera positions, enter quietly, take the goods and leave before anyone raises the alarm. If you are spotted, do not finish the robbery out of stubbornness — walk away, let things cool down, and restart the attempt fresh, because a detected robbery cannot count no matter how it ends.
steps: Choose a jewelry store and observe its staff and camera layout.
Enter quietly and avoid every line of sight.
Take the goods and exit without an alarm or a wanted spike.
The trophy unlocks once the clean robbery registers.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: vault robberies are repeatable world content tied to the completion checklist.
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time — a robbery only counts when you get away, not when you merely crack the vault. These vault jobs also sit inside the 100% checklist's robbery block (which asks for even more vault work in total), so every success here is progress twice over. Build a repeatable routine: case the bank, bring your partner and a fast getaway car staged outside, crack the vault, and have your escape route chosen before the alarm peaks.
steps: Pick a bank vault job and stage a fast car nearby.
Rob the vault with your partner.
Escape and fully lose the wanted level.
Repeat at five vaults in total; the silver unlocks on the fifth clean escape.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list
KeenGamer — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Platinum Roadmap

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: armored trucks keep spawning as world events.
trophies.guide: Rob one armored truck and escape with the take. Armored trucks appear as moving world events; when one crosses your path, disable it, deal with its guards, breach the rear doors and grab the cash, then lose the wanted level that follows. Keep a heavy weapon and a fast car ready so a chance sighting can be converted on the spot — the trophy needs a single success, and it also overlaps the robbery content counted by the 100% checklist.
steps: Watch for an armored truck event while free-roaming.
Stop the truck and neutralise its guards.
Breach the doors and take the cash.
Escape and clear your wanted level; the trophy unlocks.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: the map stays open; unexplored areas can be visited at any time.
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — the map's fog only lifts where you have actually been. Most of the state reveals itself naturally across the story, strands and collectible hunts; what remains at the end is usually a handful of remote corners, islands and back-country patches. Finish it methodically: open the map, find the still-fogged areas, and drive or fly each one until it registers. A fast aircraft makes the final sweep painless.
steps: Open the map late in your run and note every still-fogged area.
Travel through each unvisited area until it registers as explored.
Use an aircraft for islands and remote corners.
The trophy unlocks when the 52nd area is explored.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: gang operations are repeatable world content and part of the completion checklist.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation run by each of the game's 9 gangs — nine robberies, but the variety matters more than the count: hitting the same gang nine times does not advance it. Gang operations are also a named block of the 100% checklist, which asks for many more of them overall, so log which gang each operation belonged to as you go and deliberately seek out the gangs you have not yet robbed. The checklist's operation counter tells you how much total work remains even though this trophy only needs one per gang.
steps: Rob an illegal operation and note which gang owned it.
Target operations in territories of gangs you have not yet robbed.
Keep a tally until all 9 gangs have been robbed once.
The trophy unlocks on the ninth distinct gang.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list
KeenGamer — GTA 6 Trophy Guide & Platinum Roadmap

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: Ocean Beach and its bars remain accessible in free-roam.
trophies.guide: A quiet one: have a cocktail somewhere with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to the Ocean Beach strip, find a bar or spot that serves drinks with the ocean in front of you, and order a cocktail. This is a deliberate nod to the series' roots — a slow moment rather than a challenge — and it can be done at almost any point once the area is open, so slot it into any early trip to the beach rather than making a special journey.
steps: Travel to Ocean Beach.
Find a beachfront bar or drinks spot with an ocean view.
Order and enjoy a cocktail there.
The trophy unlocks as the moment registers.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: showrooms stay in the world and the stunt can be repeated.
trophies.guide: Drive a car out through a vehicle showroom's glass, in the series' classic style. Enter a showroom, get into one of its display vehicles, and accelerate straight out through the storefront rather than using the door. The moment is theatrical rather than difficult; the only ways to fail it are leaving on foot or nudging out politely, so commit to the smash. Expect a small wanted level for the damage.
steps: Enter a vehicle showroom.
Get into a display vehicle inside.
Accelerate out through the glass storefront.
The trophy unlocks as you smash out.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: the bowling alley is a permanent world location.
trophies.guide: Visit the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and bowl with a proper follow-through. This is an activity trophy in disguise: find the alley, start a game of bowling, and play your shots with the full bowling motion the game asks for. It also registers bowling among your tried activity types for Master of None, so one visit does two jobs. The description is playful rather than precise, so if a single frame does not trigger it, finish the full game before concluding anything.
steps: Travel to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Start a bowling game.
Bowl your shots with the full follow-through motion.
Finish the game if the trophy has not already popped.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.missableNote: Not missable on current information: it is tied to the partner system, which stays available; flagged honestly as a vague description.
trophies.guide: The official description — a partnership with mass appeal — is deliberately cryptic, and early guides list this among the trophies whose exact trigger is not yet fully pinned down. What is clear from the wording is that it belongs to the partner system: something the two protagonists do together that draws public attention. The practical advice is to keep doing partner activities in public settings — the paired free-roam trophies in this guide come from the same system — and to keep a manual save rotation so an unexpected one-off moment can be revisited. This guide will not invent a precise trigger the sources do not support.
steps: Keep your partner with you during free-roam sessions.
Do paired activities in busy, public places.
Keep rotating manual saves so a one-off public moment can be retried.
Watch for the unlock during partner activities; it is reported as still being pinned down by guide writers.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: choices accumulate across the whole game and PlayStation tracks a long counter for it.
trophies.guide: Make choices — for better or worse — until PlayStation's tracked counter for this trophy reaches 500. The description is vague by design, but the tracker tells the real story: this is an accumulation trophy over the game's many small decisions and interactions, not a single dramatic branch. It fills up through ordinary play if you engage with dialogue options and world interactions instead of skipping them. Check the trophy's progress bar on PlayStation to see how far along you are, and grind remaining choices through repeatable interactions late in the run if needed.
steps: Engage with dialogue and interaction choices instead of skipping them.
Check the trophy's tracked progress on PlayStation periodically.
Keep choosing during strands, activities and free-roam encounters.
Top up with repeatable interactions until the counter reaches 500.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableNote: Not missable on current information: the fail-then-succeed pattern can be produced in repeatable activities.
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: fail at something, then succeed at the same thing on the retry. Early guide coverage lists this among the trophies whose exact trigger is still being pinned down, so this guide gives the honest reading of the description rather than a fabricated one: the pattern it describes is a failed attempt followed by a successful one. Repeatable activities — races, range challenges, fishing and stunt attempts — are where fail-then-succeed naturally happens, so play them normally and note the unlock when it lands; if you want to force it, fail a short retryable activity on purpose and immediately succeed at it.
steps: Pick a short, retryable activity such as a race or range challenge.
Fail an attempt (or let a natural failure stand).
Retry the same activity and succeed.
The trophy is reported around this fail-then-succeed pattern; repeat in another activity if needed.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missableNote: Not missable on current information: strange encounters are world events that can be sought out repeatedly.
trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the game's UFO-flavoured secret. The description is a wink rather than a walkthrough, and early guides file it among the not-yet-fully-documented trophies. The series' tradition points the way: odd lights, remote locations, and the small hours of the night. Explore Leonida's remote corners after dark, investigate any unusual sighting rather than driving past it, and keep a save rotation so a one-off sighting can be chased again. This entry deliberately avoids inventing a precise location that sources have not yet confirmed.
steps: Explore remote parts of Leonida at night.
Investigate unusual lights or sightings instead of passing them by.
Stay in the area when something strange begins until it resolves.
The trophy unlocks when the encounter registers.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: the setup can be created in any crowded street in free-roam.
trophies.guide: Knock a pedestrian down with a melee drive-by — striking someone from a moving vehicle with a melee attack rather than running them over. Line up a lone pedestrian on an open pavement, approach at moderate speed (too fast and it becomes a plain collision, too slow and you will stop), and swing as you pass so the melee connects while the vehicle is moving. A quiet street with a single pedestrian is a far cleaner setup than a crowd.
steps: Find a lone pedestrian on an open pavement.
Approach at a moderate, steady speed.
Perform a melee attack from the vehicle as you pass so it connects mid-drive-by.
The trophy unlocks when the drive-by knockdown registers.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: robbery income and laundering contacts remain available in the endgame.
trophies.guide: Launder a cumulative $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from robbery work, and laundering is how they become spendable — so this trophy is really a measure of how much robbery income you have pushed through the fence system. Keep laundering as you go rather than hoarding marked cash: every robbery in the 100% sweep feeds it. Note that some fences disappear as the story progresses, but guides confirm new ones unlock to replace them, so the laundering route never closes.
steps: Earn Marked Bills from robberies and heists.
Take them to a laundering contact promptly instead of hoarding them.
Repeat robbery-and-launder cycles during the 100% sweep.
The trophy unlocks when the laundered total reaches $250,000.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: shops stay open and endgame income makes the total reachable.
trophies.guide: Spend a cumulative $100,000 across all shops. This is an endgame economy trophy: early on, $100,000 is real money, but robbery and laundering income through the 100% sweep makes it a formality. Spend naturally on vehicles, weapons, upgrades and property dressing as you play, and if you reach the late game short of the mark, buy the expensive items you were postponing anyway rather than wasting cash on junk — the counter only cares about the total spent.
steps: Buy weapons, upgrades and vehicles as you progress instead of hoarding cash.
Track your lifetime spend if the game shows it, or estimate from big purchases.
In the endgame, clear the remaining total with high-value purchases you actually want.
The trophy unlocks when cumulative shop spending reaches $100,000.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: properties remain purchasable in free-roam once unlocked.
trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties on the map. Garages unlock as purchases through the game's property system; work through the property listings, buy each garage as your income allows, and save the most expensive for the endgame when robbery money is plentiful. This pairs with Treat Yo Self, since property spending is exactly the kind of big-ticket purchase that clears that counter, and with the vehicle trophies, since garages give your discovered vehicles somewhere to live.
steps: Open the property listings and note all 8 garage locations.
Buy garages as robbery income allows, cheapest first.
Clear the last expensive garages in the endgame.
The trophy unlocks when the eighth garage is purchased.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.missableNote: Not missable: vehicles and the app remain available throughout.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Whenever you acquire a vehicle you intend to keep, register it in the app there and then — ten registrations accumulate quickly if the habit forms early, especially alongside Whip It Good's 100-vehicle discovery hunt, which constantly puts new vehicles in your hands. If you reach the endgame short, simply acquire and register vehicles in a batch until the counter fills.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app when you acquire a vehicle you will keep.
Register the vehicle in the app.
Repeat with each new keeper, especially while hunting the 100 discovered vehicles.
The trophy unlocks at the tenth registration.
sources: Exophase — GTA VI PSN trophy list
